problems.question:
Given three sets \(A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\},\; B = \{1, 3, 5, 7\}\) and \( C = \{1, 4, 6, 7\},\) what is \((A ∪ B) ∩ C?\)

［作答］

\(\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\} \)

［作答］

\(\{1, 4, 7\} \)

［作答］

\(\{1, 3\}\)

［作答］

\( \{6\} \)
problems.solution: The union of \(A\) and \( B\) is the set whose members belong to\( A\) or \( B\) (or both \( A \) and \( B\)), so \( A ∪ B = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7\}.\) The intersection of \( A ∪ B\; \text{and}\; C \) is the set whose members belong to both \(A ∪ B \) and \( C,\) so \((A ∪ B) ∩ C = \{1, 4, 7\}.\)
problems.title: Question 1

problems.question:
Given the set \( A =\{n: \text{n is a whole number and}\; 5 < n ≤ 13\},\) select all the sets below that are subsets of \(A.\)

［作答］

\((5, 13]\)

［作答］

\(\{5, 6, 11, 13\} \)

［作答］

\(\{7\}\)

［作答］

\(\{n :\text{n is a whole number and}\; 6 ≤ n < 14\}\)
problems.solution: The set \((5, 13]\) contains elements that are not in \(A\) (since it contains all real numbers that are greater than 5 and less than or equal to 13), so it is not a subset of \(A.\) The set \(\{5, 6, 11, 13\}\) contains the number 5 which is not a member of \(A\) and so \(\{5, 6, 11, 13\}\) is not a subset of \(A.\) The set \(\{7\}\) is clearly a subset of \(A\) since \( 7 ∈ A,\) and the fourth set is equal to \(A\) (just described in a different way) and so it is also a subset of \(A\)
problems.title: Question 2

problems.question:
Given the sets \(A = \{x\; |\;x \text{ is a whole number and}\; x > −1\}\) and \(B = \{x\; |\; x \text{ is a whole number and}\; x < 2\} ,\)which of the sets below is equal to \(A ∩ B\)?

［作答］

\((−1, 2)\)

［作答］

\([0, 1]\)

［作答］

\(\{0, 1\}\)

［作答］

\((−∞,∞)\)
problems.solution: We note that \(A = \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, . . . \}\) and \(B = \{. . . , −3, −2, −1, 0, 1\}\) and therefore \(A ∩ B = \{0, 1\}.\) As a side note, the sets \((−1, 2), [0, 1] \) and \( (−∞,∞)\) all contain numbers that are not whole numbers, which immediately excludes the possibility of these being correct answers.
problems.title: Question 3

problems.question:
Consider the function \(f\) from \(\mathbb{R}\) to \(\mathbb{R}\) given by \(f(x) = 2x − 5.\) Find the real numbers \(a\) and \(b\) such that a formula for the inverse function \(f^{−1}\) is given by \(f^{−1}(x) = ax+b.\)

\(a =\)

［作答］ correct

1/2

\(\frac{1}{2}\)

\(b =\)

［作答］ correct

5/2

\(\frac{5}{2}\)
problems.solution: Writing \(y = 2x − 5\) and solving for \(x\) in terms of \(y,\) we find that \(x =\frac{y + 5}{2}\) and therefore \(f^{−1}(y) = \frac{y + 5}{2}\) . Since we were asked to give the formula for\(f^{−1}\) in terms of \(x,\) we replace \(y\) by \(x\) to get the final answer.
problems.title: Question 4

problems.question:
If \(f(x) = 2x + 7 \) and \( g(x) = x − 4,\) find the real numbers \(a\) and \(b\) such that a formula for the inverse \((fg)^{−1}\) of the composition \(fg\) is given by \((fg)^{−1}(x) = ax + b.\)

\(a =\)

［作答］ correct

1/2

\(\frac{1}{2}\)

\(b =\)

［作答］ correct

1/2

\(\frac{1}{2}\)
problems.solution: We have \(fg(x) = f(x − 4) = 2(x − 4) + 7 = 2x − 1.\) Hence, writing \( y = 2x − 1\) and solving for \(x\) in terms of \(y,\) we find that \(x =\frac{y + 1}{2}\) and so\((fg)^{−1}(y) =\frac{y+1}{2}.\) Since we were asked to give the formula for \((fg)^{-1}\) in terms of \(x,\) we replace \(y\) by \(x\) to get the final answer.

collected.content:
A set may be thought of as a collection of objects.

A set is usually described by listing or describing its members inside curly brackets. For example, when we write \(A = \{1, 2, 3\}\), we mean that the objects belonging to the set \(A\) are the numbers 1, 2, 3 (or, equivalently, the set \(A\) consists of the numbers 1, 2 and 3).

When \(x\) is an object in a set \(A\), we write \(x \in A\) and say ‘\(x\) belongs to \(A\)’ or ‘\(x\) is a member of \(A\)’.

The set which has no members is called the empty set and is denoted by \(\emptyset\). The empty set may seem like a strange concept, but it has its uses.

We say that the set \(S\) is a subset of the set \(T\), and we write \(S \subseteq T\), if every member of \(S\) is a member of \(T\). For example, \(\{1, 2, 3\} \subseteq \{1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 40\}\). (Be aware that some texts use \(\subset\) where we use \(\subseteq\).)

The main topics studied in Module 1 are:

  • sets
  • special sets of numbers and their notations
  • the meaning of a function
  • inverse functions: what they mean and how to find them when they exist
  • the composition of two functions: what it means and how to find a formula for a composition
  • what is meant by the graph of a function
  • how to solve quadratic equations: factorisation, the formula for a solution, and completing the square
  • how to sketch the graphs of linear and quadratic functions
  • power functions and exponential functions
  • logarithms and the natural logarithm
  • trigonometrical functions: radians, graphs of the trigonometrical functions, and trigonometrical identities
  • finding the intersection of two graphs
  • sketching supply and demand curves, and finding equilibrium.
